title: Prompt ensembling: combining several prompts and voting

videos.script: Ask three times and take the answer most of them gave. On paper that is a large gain. Three voters who are each right eighty percent of the time make a majority that is right almost ninety. {{arithmetic}} That sum has one condition, and this lesson is about the condition. The voters have to make different mistakes. {{independent}} You vote three of this course's prompts over seventy messages. The best of them gets fifty-four right, and the vote gets forty-nine. Twelve messages were wrong under all three prompts, and no vote can fix those. {{three}} Then you vote five samples of one prompt at a high temperature. The vote gets one message more than a single call at temperature zero, and that message was a formatting bug, not a hard label. {{samples}} Finally you put a price on it, because every voter is another call. By the end you can tell when a vote is worth paying for, and you know what to compare it with. {{close}}
